full_judgment:
2. In Writ Petition No. 9157 of 2005 the petitioners have called in question the decision to prepare a fresh Electoral Roll taken by the respondent No. 2 without consent of the two other commissioners and also appointment given by the respondent No.3 to about 2,40,000 Enumerators, 70,000 Supervisors, 6235 Assistant Registration Officers and 83 Registration Officers pursuant to the impugned decision. The decision referred to in the writ petition has been annexed as Annexure-A to the writ petition and on perusal of the same we found that Annexure-A is not a decision of fresh voter list. Since at the time of hearing the Chief Election Commissioner was being represented by his lawyer, learned Senior Counsel Mr Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the Court put a question to him whether in fact there was a decision for fresh voter list and the answer being in the affirmative the Court directed him to produce the relevant decision which eventually was submitted by submitting Affidavit-of-Compliance also annexing the connected records. From that Affidavit-of-Compliance, it appears that the commission took a decision as per Annexure-1 of that Affidavit-of-Compliance and other relevant papers are regarding the process leading to the ultimate meeting held on 6th of August, 2005 as evidenced by Annexures-I to IV to the Affidavit-of-Compliance. 

 ১। ভোটার তালিকা অধ্যদেশ ,১৯৮২ (Electoral Rolls Ordinance 1982) এবং ভোটার তালিকা বিধিমালা ১৯৮২ (Electoral Rolls Ordinance 1982) অনুসারে নতুনভাবে ভোটার তালকা প্রণয়নের লক্ষে তথ্য সংগ্রহকারী ও সুপারভাইজারগন বাড়ী বাড়ী গিয়ে ভোটার হওয়ার যোগ্য ব্যক্তিদের তথ্য সংগ্রহ পূর্বক ভোটার তালিকা প্রণয়ন করা সিদ্ধান্ত গৃহীত হয়। স্বাধীনতার পর উপরোল্লিখিত আইন ও বিধি/অনুরুপ আইন ও বিধি Bangladesh Electoral Rolls Order 1972 and Bangladesh Electoral Rolls, Rules 1972 and Electoral Rolls Ordinance 1976  and Electoral Rolls Rules, 1976) অনুসারে ১৯৭৩ সনে ১৯৭৬ সনে ১৯৮৩ সনে ১৯৯০ সনে ও ১৯৯৫ সনে সারাদেশে ভোটার তালিকা প্রণয়ন করা হয়েছিল। তাছাড়া ১৯৯২ সনে শুধু মাত্র পৌর এলা্কায় ভোটার তালিকা প্রণয়ন করা হই্য়াছিল । সর্বশেষ ২০০০ সনে বিদ্যমান ভোটার তালিকা প্রণয়ন করা হয়েছে। অর্থাৎ জাতীয় সংসদের সাধারন নির্বাচন পূর্বে নতুন করে ভোটার তলিকা প্রণয়ন করা হয়েছে। 

 9. Now, the first question is, whether the decision was taken in the meeting of the 6th August was unilateral or was by the Commission and the second question is, whether a fresh or a new voter list is at all permissible to be prepared under the provisions of the Electoral Roll Ordinance, 1982 and the Rules thereunder or the list can be corrected, amended or revised. 

 "5. Preparation of electoral rolls—For the purpose of election to different elective bodies, there shall be prepared electoral rolls for each electoral area or constituency, as the case may be upon registration of the voters." 

 (1). The Commission shall appoint a Registration Officer for each (electoral area or constituency) for their purpose of preparation, correction, amendment and revision of an electoral roll for that (electoral area or constituency) and may, for that purpose, appoint as many Assistant Registration Officers as may be necessary, and the same person may be appointed as Registration Officer or Assistant Registration Officer for two or more (electoral areas or constituencies) 

 (2). Thus it appears from the scheme of sections 5 and 6 read together that the authority of preparation of a list vests in the Commission and the Commission may prepare a list or correct the existing list or amended the existing list or revise the list as may be deemed necessary. The word preparation has not been defined. The word preparation means action or process of preparing something. For example, preparation of meals by a cook or preparation of penicillin in a laboratory by a student. The word prepare means to get ready or make ready. In both cases neither the cook nor the student prepares out of nothing. They make the use of materials already available and if something is wanting they rush to collect it. The legislature in their wisdom used separate expression for preparation than correction and then amendment and then revision of a electoral roll as the purposes of the Registration Officers in section 6. 

 "7. Preparation and publication of electoral rolls— 

 (1) The Registration Officer for an (electoral area or constituency) shall, under the superintendence, direction and control of the Commission, prepare for that (electoral area or constituency) in the prescribed manner a draft electoral roll containing the name of every person who, on the qualifying date:— 

 (2). The draft electoral roll prepared under sub-section (1), together with a notice inviting claims and objections with respect there to, shall be published in such manner as may be prescribed. 

 (3). The Registration Officer shall, in the prescribed manner, make such additions, modifications or corrections in the draft electoral roll as may be required by any decision on any claim or objection or as may be necessary for correction of any clerical, printing or other error. 

 (4). After making additions, modifications or corrections, if any, under sub-section (3), the Registration Officer shall, in the prescribed manner, publish the final electoral rolls so published shall be the electoral roll for those electoral areas (or that constituency). 

 (5). The final electoral roll published under sub-section (4) shall come into force immediately on such publication. 

 (6). An electoral roll shall be maintained in the prescribed manner and shall be kept open for public inspection, and copies of such roll shall be supplied to any person applying therefore on payment of such fee as may be prescribed. 

 (7). If the Commission, on account of any gross error or irregularity in or in the preparation of any electoral roll for any (electoral area or constituency) or draft thereof considers it necessary so to do, it may by order direct that such roll or draft shall stand cancelled and that an electoral roll for that (electoral area or constituency) be prepared afresh. 

 (8). The Commission may cause the electoral rolls to be regrouped, if necessary, for the purpose of election to different (elective bodies)" 

 14. From a reading of the section 7 as quoted above it appears that Registration Officer so appointed must prepare a draft electoral roll containing the names of every person who is a citizen not less than 18 years of age, not declared by a competent Court to be of unsound mind and is a resident or deemed to be a resident of that area on the qualifying date and the person qualified to be a voter under Article 122 of the Constitution read with section 7(1) of the Ordinance is entitled to be a voter in the draft electoral roll to be prepared taking the list maintained under section 7(6) of the Ordinance as the major basis. Therefore, the preparation of the electoral roll means preparation of a roll taking the roll under section 7(4) and published under section 7(5) it becomes the final electoral roll but that final roll or even a draft roll for a particular area or constituency may be cancelled and a fresh roll may be prepared for that area or constituency only. 

 15. Section 10 of the Ordinance provides for amendment and correction of electoral rolls and section 11 provides for revision of the rolls. The expression "unless otherwise directed by the Commission" in section 11(1)(a) of the Ordinance is a sufficient indication that other than revision the Commission can follow the foregoing procedure as in sections 5 and 7 for preparation of electoral rolls. We must not lose sight of the chronology of section 7 which puts final roll in section 7(5) and roll afresh of an area or constituency in section 7(7) and up-dating and revision in section 10 and 11 respectively of the Ordinance. 

 16. It thus follows that the decision in the meeting, of 6th August 2005 was not unilateral rather it was decision of the Commissioner and the commission is required to have an electoral roll prepared as distinguished from mere corrected, amended or revised taking the list maintained under section 7(6) of the Ordinance as the major basis. The confusion as to the name as new list, fresh list or revised list about the electoral roll is of no significance because, "what is in a name", it remains the electoral roll prepared under the law by whatever name it is called. 

 19. The file further reveals that the Election Commissioner No.1 could not be approached as he was in the hospital. Then the Chief Election Commissioner on the same date writes, "All the members of the Commission in a meeting held on the 6th August, 2005 signed on 7-8-2005 agreed that the voters list for the 9th Parliamentary Election shall be prepared in accordance with the voters list Ordinance, 1992 and the Electoral Roll Rules of 1982 which were prepared in the light of the voters list prepared in 1983, 1990, 1992, 1995 and 2006 respectively by collecting data of all the eligible others through door-to-door visit by enumerators (the decision of the commission dated 7-8-2005 as aforesaid is at page 14 of the file signed by Election Commissioners 1 and 2 respectively). Hence the note of dissent at paragraph 12 is a travesty of the truth. Accordingly, the proposal in paragraph-11 is approved in accordance with the decision of the Election Commission." 

 24. Mr Khandoker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the Election Commission, however, submitted that the Electoral Rolls is being prepared as per law and practice and the existing Electoral Roll is not at all being abandoned and is in the process of preparation and the apprehensions are totally unfounded. 

 27. In view of the provisions of section 7(6) of the Ordinance the Commission must maintain an Electoral Roll which must hold the field till the publication of the Electoral Roll prepared by the Commission and the Election Commission cannot be oblivious of the existing list. The voters whose names appear in the existing roll cannot be dropped unless one is dead, declared to be of unsound mind by a competent Court or has ceased to be resident or ceased to be deemed to be a resident of that area or constituency. The right to be a voter under Article 122 read with section 7(1) of the Ordinance cannot be made dependent on his being present when the Enumerators visit his house or on his signature in a particular form. It is unlikely that the Commission will not be oblivious of the facts that thousands of Hajees including some Justices of this Court are out of the country at the moment while such a roll is under preparation not it is permissible to drop them from the existing roll only on the ground that they are absent and cannot sign the forms. 

 29. The papers produced before us give a dismal picture of the Election Commission. The Commission took a decision in the meeting held on 6th of August for preparation of Electoral Roll and appointment of Registration Officer, etc but subsequently the Chief Election Commissioner is claiming that the decision was for fresh list while another Commissioner is claiming that it was for a revised list. Yet another Commissioner is claiming against records that no such decision was taken on 6th of August Another Commissioner Mr AK Mohammad Ali is telling the press on 2nd of October, 2005 as evidenced by Annexure-D to the writ petition in Writ Petition 9157 that they did not support the last meeting decision. Mr MM Munsef Ali and he had suggested that the voter list should be revised whereas he is making such a note on 5th of October in the file. How the press could know about his decision of 5th October on 2nd of October, 2005. 

 30. The Commission is vested with the task of preparing the electoral roll as per law. It is the commission to decide whether the Electoral Roll should be prepared or corrected and amended or revised but it appears that the Commission is sharing the opinion of the political parties as to what to do creating a scope for controversies which should have been avoided. 

 (1) It is held that the decision for preparation of Electoral Roll taken in the meeting on 6th August, 2005 was not unilateral decision of the Chief Election Commissioner, rather it was a decision of the Commission for the preparation of the Electoral Roll and appointment of the Registration Officers, etc. 

 (3) The Commission should prepare the Electoral Roll taking the existing Roll maintained under section 7(6) of the Ordinance as a major basis. 

 If there is a computerised database the Commission should make the best use of it and if not, a computerised Electoral Roll with database should always be maintained to avoid future controversy, costs and labour. 

 (4) The persons whose names are already in the existing electoral roll cannot be dropped from that roll unless they are dead or have been declared to be of unsound mind or ceased to be residents or ceased to be deemed to be residents of that area or the constituency. 

 (5) The Chief Election Commissioner should immediately call a meeting of the Commission and the Commission should decide and take all appropriate steps to implement the decision of the Commission taken on 6th of August, 2005 in its meeting for preparation of Electoral Roll in the light of this judgment. 

 Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the Election Commission, Bangladesh by Special Messenger. The Election Commission should publish a copy of this judgment in the leading daily newspapers to dispel all doubts about the preparation of the Electoral Roll which is going on.
